topSignals.title: New Mexico Supreme Court grants stay, pausing both Project Jupiter proceedings.
topSignals.text: Ruling Sunday, August 23 (reported August 24), the Court unanimously paused the NMED air-quality permit hearing and the emergency water-well authorization for Oracle's 2.45 GW Bloom SOFC data center in Santa Teresa, resolving for now the two petitions this digest has tracked since August 19-20. The State Engineer and NMED must respond by September 2. If the stay holds, the September 14 hearing cannot proceed as scheduled, pushing the permitting track past SemiAnalysis's 2029 first-power base case. KVIA | NM Political Report

topSignals.title: PJM's capacity backstop gets a hard price ceiling: $555/MW-day, up from $325.
topSignals.text: A deeper read of PJM's Reliability Backstop Procurement (FERC Docket ER26-3380) shows a two-track design: a bilateral-matching window already open since August 2026 for data centers to contract directly with new supply, and a residual auction (bid window September 30 to October 21, results by December 2) capped at $555/MW-day in UCAP terms for contracts up to 15 years, up from the $325/MW-day cap the last base auction hit across its entire footprint. NRDC estimates PJM could pay up to $20 billion for new plants under the mechanism. A usable ceiling for benchmarking behind-the-meter SOFC against the cost of staying grid-connected in PJM territory, see LCOE section below. Electron Economics | Utility Dive

topSignals.title: TerraPower names Hyundai E&C as EPC for up to 8 Natrium reactors, SK Innovation deal alongside (August 14, first appearance).
topSignals.text: Announced during a Seoul trip by Bill Gates and CEO Chris Levesque with Korea's Prime Minister, HD Hyundai, HDEC, SK Innovation and the Export-Import Bank of Korea, TerraPower named Hyundai Engineering & Construction EPC contractor for up to eight future Natrium plants (345 MW sodium-cooled fast reactor plus molten-salt storage, peaking to 500 MW), with completion, price and performance guarantees. A firmer commercialization step than the non-binding Holtec/Entergy/Hyundai Gulf South MOA already on file, though first power still runs into the 2030s, leaving SOFC's near-term deployment-speed advantage intact. World Nuclear News | TerraPower | UPI

SOEC side only, consistent with Sunfire's 2024 exit from the SOFC/fuel-cell business already on file. Renewable Energy Magazine | gasworld

lcoe.text: PJM backstop price ceiling as an avoided-cost benchmark (✎ my calculation from PJM's reported figures, not a primary-sourced number): $555/MW-day works out to about $202.6/kW-year ($555 x 365 days), versus roughly $118.6/kW-year at the prior $325/MW-day base-auction cap. That is a usable ceiling for what a PJM-territory data center might otherwise pay for capacity if it stays grid-connected, i.e. the avoided-cost benchmark that behind-the-meter SOFC economics need to beat, on top of avoided energy costs. See Top Signal #2.
Gas price case: EIA's August STEO figures ($3.44/MMBtu 2026 average, $3.03/MMBtu for the remaining five months) are unchanged from the August 25 flag; no new revision today.
